title: Corotating gas drag gives a growing mode at the synchronous radius in a finite-field dust model
abstract: We test whether gas drag makes charged dust settle at a corotating magnetic site. In an ideal prescribed magnetosphere, electric and magnetic forces cancel for a grain at rest in the rotating frame. With central gravity, an exact rest equilibrium lies on the synchronous ring. We prove that symmetric positive definite drag toward rigidly rotating gas gives this equilibrium a positive real growth rate for any smooth finite local magnetic field. The determinant has derivative -3 Gamma_yy at zero in normalized units. For a vertical field, an exact cubic gives the growing rate and an analytic minimum growth time over drag strength. A published hot-corona benchmark gives growth e-folding times of 12.92 rotations for a 1 micrometre grain and 92.59 rotations for a 0.5 micrometre grain at one magnetic polarity. These are model values, not measured CPV lifetimes. In the magnetic slow-mode limit, fixed-drag contraction gives a time proportional to x^-6 and the adopted grain prescription gives a^-3. The powers do not imply an occurrence law. Symbolic checks, 2,573 linear comparisons, 2,000 arbitrary-field and drag cases, and six full dipole orbits verify the calculations. Planetary dust drift and dissipation-induced instability are prior work; the contribution is the explicit CPV stability diagnostic, exact bounds and reproducible calculations. Gas response, extra electric forces, finite gyro energy and differential gas rotation can change the result. No external record data are bundled.

display.caption: Exact growth e-folding time in rotation periods over signed vertical field and isotropic drag. Every finite plotted field with positive drag has a growing mode. Contours give 1, 10, 100 and 1,000 periods; orange stars mark the 1 micrometre hot-corona example.

Exact growth time as the stellar radius changes at fixed mass, period, surface field and gas state. The inverse-sixth-power limit holds only when the magnetic term dominates. No CPV rate or lifetime is fitted.

Six full nonlinear dipole orbits recover the local growing mode over 4.6 e-folds, with displacements from 1e-6 to about 1e-4 corotation radii. These are local checks, not full cloud escape simulations.
